items.title: Two Mississauga developments could add hundreds of new residents to existing neighbourhoods
items.summary: Two proposed residential developments that could bring more than 150 townhouses to existing apartment properties in Mississauga are being put before residents, with a city councillor arranging back-to-back community meetings to explain the plans and hear concerns. The proposals, both involving property owner and developer CAPREIT, would add new townhouse developments at 1055 Bloor Street and 2121 Rathburn Road East. Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca has invited residents to meet with the developers and City of Mississauga staff to learn more about the projects, ask questions and discuss how the additions could affect their neighbourhoods. m. in the Fleetwood Village Room at Burnhamthorpe Community Centre, 1500 Gulleden Drive. The discussion will focus on 1055 Bloor Street, where CAPREIT is proposing to add 112 stacked townhouse units to an existing apartment property. The proposal has already encountered some planning hurdles. On August 20, the application appeared before the City’s Committee of Adjustment seeking 19 variances to allow the development to proceed. According to Fonseca, city planning staff and committee members raised concerns about the proposal, including parking and potential traffic impacts. The staff report recommended deferring the application, and the committee directed the applicant to work with the councillor’s office and the surrounding community before returning.

items.title: One Mississauga man’s efforts have brought cricket to thousands of students
items.summary: For years, cricket was familiar to many newcomer families in Mississauga, but their children couldn’t always play it through school. One local volunteer set out to change that, bringing the sport into school gyms and physical education programs and giving thousands of students a chance to participate. Ranil Mendis has spent more than three decades working to expand access to cricket, building partnerships with school boards, educators, municipalities and community organizations along the way. His efforts have helped grow school cricket into an organized program reaching more than 5,000 Ontario students annually, according to the Ontario Schools Cricket Association (OSCA), where Mendis serves as a board member. The work has now earned him one of Mississauga’s highest community honours. Mendis was recently named the recipient of the 2026 Gordon S. Shipp Memorial Award for Citizen of the Year. But the recognition also shines a light on an initiative that has grown considerably since its early days. The roots of the school cricket program go back to the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants (CIMA) Canada, which developed a community initiative to introduce the sport to students from diverse backgrounds. Mendis helped lead the effort, working with school boards and other partners to overcome some of the barriers that had kept cricket out of many schools.

items.title: When will your street get plowed? Here’s how Mississauga handles winter snow
items.summary: With snow looming in the forecast, Mississauga residents may soon be watching for snowplows as the city prepares to clear roads, sidewalks and other public spaces across the city. The City of Mississauga has crews ready around the clock to deal with winter weather, but not every street gets plowed at the same time. The municipality follows a priority system that determines which roads and sidewalks are cleared first and how long residents may have to wait for their neighbourhood streets. The first priority is keeping major routes safe and accessible for emergency vehicles, public transit and motorists. That includes major roads, priority sidewalks, bus stops, pedestrian crossings, roadside multi-use trails and on-street bike lanes. Parking lots and entrances connected to community centres, arenas and libraries are also included in the initial clearing operations. Once the priority routes have been dealt with, crews move on to residential roads and secondary sidewalks. The city says priority roads and sidewalks can take between 12 and 24 hours to clear after snowfall stops. Residential roads and secondary sidewalks are generally cleared within 24 to 36 hours. However, those timelines can be extended when Mississauga experiences back-to-back snowstorms or a major snowfall of more than 30 centimetres. Residents should also be aware that residential streets are not cleared down to bare pavement. Crews aim to make them safe and passable for vehicles, meaning some packed snow may remain.

items.title: Landmark railway bridge could be demolished in Mississauga
items.summary: A landmark railway bridge could be demolished in Mississauga. Metrolinx is preparing to demolish the Credit River Railway Bridge, which spans the river in Port Credit, just west of the Port Credit GO Station, according to a letter from Giaimo + Associates Architects Inc. to the Town of Port Credit Association. Giaimo said it has been retained by Metrolinx to prepare a Heritage Impact Assessment on the bridge. Originally built in 1903 and twinned in 2008, the bridge is now owned by Metrolinx. The bridge carries two railway tracks in an east-west direction across the Credit River, between Stavebank Road and Mississauga Road. The Credit River Bridge is comprised of “a central deck truss bridge of unusual design with two approach beam spans,” according to a 2017 Metrolinx report. Giaimo said Metrolinx conducted detailed structural inspections of the bridge to assess the condition and recommend potential rehabilitation options. “The bridge was found to be in poor condition, and it was determined that the existing structure could not be rehabilitated,” Giaimo said in the letter. The bridge carries GO Transit, VIA and freight rail operations and must continue to accommodate existing service requirements and future GO service expansion while meeting Transport Canada requirements.

items.title: Hospitality Worker Collects $7-Million Lump Sum After Winning Daily Grand's Top Prize
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Mississauga hospitality worker James Lui-Yee won the Daily Grand's top prize of $1,000 a day for life, but chose the $7 million lump sum payout instead. The outlet reported the winning ticket was purchased at a Petro-Canada on Burnhamthorpe Road West. Lui-Yee said he did not check the ticket until two weeks after the draw and initially thought the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation app had made an error. He said his heart raced once he manually confirmed his numbers matched the winning combination at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto. Lui-Yee said he plans to seek financial advice before making major decisions, but hopes to buy a home, invest and travel to Greece, Portugal and Spain, Mississauga.com reported. He also looks forward to buying a new phone and an advanced chessboard, according to the outlet.

items.title: Use-of-Force Training and Anti-Black Racism Among Issues as Francique Inquest Opens
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique has begun after being delayed a day from its original Thursday start. The outlet reported Francique, a 28-year-old Black man, was shot by Peel Regional Police during an attempted arrest outside his home on Jan. 7, 2020, and died in hospital days later. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit later cleared the officers, saying the officer who fired reported fearing for his life after Francique drove toward him, the Star said. The SIU noted there were still questions about the officer's conduct, including his decision to position himself near a fleeing vehicle, according to the report. The inquest will examine police procedures on use of force involving vehicles, oversight of planned arrests, medical care for incapacitated suspects and anti-Black racism, the Toronto Star reported.

items.title: Driver in Custody After Truck Hits Boston Pizza and Police Cruiser at Square One
items.summary: According to insauga.com, a truck crashed into the Boston Pizza restaurant at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga early Friday morning. The outlet reported the vehicle also collided with a police cruiser before the driver was taken into custody. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told insauga.com that officers did not identify the driver beyond confirming he is an adult male. Insauga.com said there is no word yet on potential charges. Photos from the scene showed significant damage to the restaurant, including a section of broken windows, according to the outlet.

items.title: Shape the future of your community by serving on a Committee of Council
items.summary: Applications are open from November 13 to December 4, 2026. Looking for a way to make a difference in your community? The City of Mississauga is inviting residents to serve on select committees, local boards and authorities to help guide City decisions and advise Council on key issues. Applications will be accepted from November 13 to December 4, 2026. There are several committees and boards seeking citizen members, including the Accessibility Advisory Committee, Mississauga Appeals and Property Standards Committee, Committee of Adjustment, Mississauga Arts Council, Mississauga Library Board and the Greater Toronto Airports Authority (GTAA) Consultative Committee. Members are asked to serve a four-year term ending on November 14, 2030. The City is hosting a drop-in information session for those interested in learning more about the committees noted above and the application process.
